trials.population: Advanced pancreatic NET (RADIANT-3, SUN) / lung-GI NET (RADIANT-4)
trials.result: RADIANT-3 mPFS 11.0 vs 4.6 mo; sunitinib 11.4 vs 5.5 mo
trials.takeaway: Everolimus and sunitinib are standard for progressive pNET.

inclusion: Advanced pancreatic (RADIANT-3, SUN) or lung/GI NET (RADIANT-4)
appraisal.critique: Everolimus and sunitinib are options after SSAs, chosen by site and toxicity profile. Neither improved OS significantly.

trials.name: E2211 (CAPTEM)
trials.takeaway: CAPTEM is an active cytotoxic option for pNET.

appraisal.critique: CAPTEM improves PFS and OS over temozolomide alone in pancreatic NETs. It is an inexpensive oral regimen well suited to Indian practice.

trials.name: PIVOT / ProtecT
trials.result: 15-y PCa mortality ~3% in all arms; metastasis higher with monitoring
trials.takeaway: Active surveillance is safe for low-risk disease; treatment reduces progression, not death.

limitations: Mostly low-risk disease; monitoring less rigorous than modern active surveillance (no MRI)
appraisal.critique: No prostate cancer mortality difference at 15 years, but more progression and metastasis with monitoring. Each treatment has a distinct toxicity profile, making shared decisions essential.

trials.name: RTOG 94-08
trials.result: 10-y OS 62% vs 57%; benefit in intermediate risk
trials.takeaway: Short-term ADT with RT for intermediate-risk disease.

strengths: OS benefit for short-term ADT with RT (10-year OS 62% vs 57%)
limitations: RT dose 66.6 Gy — below modern dose-escalated standards
appraisal.critique: Short-course ADT benefits intermediate-risk disease; with modern dose escalation its magnitude is debated, and favourable intermediate risk may skip it.

trials.name: Bolla EORTC 22863
trials.takeaway: Long-term ADT (2–3 y) with RT is standard for high-risk disease.

inclusion: Locally advanced (T3–4) or high-grade T1–2 prostate cancer
strengths: OS benefit for long-term ADT with RT
appraisal.critique: Established long-term ADT with RT for high-risk prostate cancer. The RT dose (70 Gy) is lower than modern standards, but the benefit of 2–3 years ADT has been confirmed in later trials.

trials.name: CHHiP
trials.result: 5-y freedom from failure 88.3% (74 Gy) vs 90.6% (60 Gy) vs 85.9% (57 Gy)
trials.takeaway: 60 Gy/20 fr moderate hypofractionation is a standard.

appraisal.critique: 60 Gy in 20 fractions is now standard moderate hypofractionation, saving three weeks of treatment. Most patients also received short-course ADT, which may have influenced outcomes.

trials.name: HYPO-RT-PC / PACE-B
trials.takeaway: 5-fraction SBRT is a standard option for low/intermediate-risk disease.

limitations: Higher acute GU toxicity in HYPO-RT-PC
appraisal.critique: Five-fraction SBRT is a standard option for low- and intermediate-risk prostate cancer, with non-inferior biochemical control. Higher acute urinary toxicity in HYPO-RT-PC was transient.

trials.name: ASCENDE-RT
trials.result: 9-y bPFS 83% vs 62%; more GU toxicity with boost
trials.takeaway: Brachytherapy boost improves biochemical control.

inclusion: Intermediate or high-risk localised prostate cancer
strengths: Improved biochemical control with LDR boost
appraisal.critique: LDR brachytherapy boost nearly halved biochemical failure. Higher late urinary toxicity and lack of OS benefit mean careful patient selection.

trials.name: RADICALS-RT / RAVES / GETUG-AFU 17 (ARTISTIC)
trials.population: After radical prostatectomy with adverse features
arms: Early salvage RT on PSA rise
trials.result: No EFS benefit with adjuvant RT; early salvage avoided RT in ~half
trials.takeaway: Early salvage RT is preferred over routine adjuvant RT.

inclusion: After radical prostatectomy with adverse features (pT3/4, positive margins)
strengths: Meta-analysis showed early salvage equivalent to adjuvant RT
appraisal.critique: Early salvage RT is preferred over routine adjuvant RT after prostatectomy, avoiding RT in many men. Few very high-risk patients were included, so adjuvant RT may still benefit them.

trials.name: STAMPEDE (arm H) M1 RT
trials.result: Low-volume: 3-y OS 81% vs 73% (HR 0.68); no benefit in high-volume
trials.takeaway: Prostate RT for low-volume mHSPC.

inclusion: Newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
strengths: OS benefit for low metastatic burden
limitations: Burden defined by CHAARTED criteria on conventional imaging
appraisal.critique: Prostate RT improves OS in low-volume mHSPC. It is not effective in high-volume disease; volume is defined by conventional imaging, not PSMA-PET.

trials.name: CHAARTED
trials.result: mOS 57.6 vs 44.0 mo; benefit in high-volume (HR 0.63)
trials.takeaway: Docetaxel with ADT for high-volume mHSPC.

appraisal.critique: Docetaxel with ADT improves OS in high-volume mHSPC, but not clearly in low-volume disease. Triplet therapy has since evolved from this foundation.

trials.name: LATITUDE / STAMPEDE abiraterone
trials.takeaway: Abiraterone with ADT for mHSPC.

appraisal.critique: Abiraterone with ADT improves OS in high-risk mHSPC. Inexpensive generics make it highly relevant in India, but hypertension and hypokalaemia need monitoring.

trials.name: TITAN / ENZAMET / ARCHES
trials.result: TITAN OS HR 0.65; ENZAMET 5-y OS 67% vs 57%
trials.takeaway: ARPI intensification for all fit mHSPC patients.

appraisal.critique: ARPIs with ADT improve OS in mHSPC across disease volumes. Fatigue, falls and cost are the main considerations.

trials.name: PEACE-1 / ARASENS
trials.result: ARASENS OS HR 0.68; PEACE-1 high-volume OS HR 0.72
trials.takeaway: Triplet therapy for fit high-volume de novo mHSPC.

appraisal.critique: Triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + ARPI) improves OS over ADT + docetaxel in de novo mHSPC. No trial compares triplet with ADT + ARPI doublet, which is the key unanswered question.

trials.name: SPARTAN / PROSPER / ARAMIS
trials.population: nmCRPC with PSA doubling time ≤10 mo
trials.result: MFS gain ~2 years (HR ~0.3); OS benefit in all three
trials.takeaway: ARPI for high-risk nmCRPC.

inclusion: nmCRPC with PSA doubling time ≤10 months
limitations: PSMA-PET would reclassify many patients as metastatic
appraisal.critique: ARPIs delay metastasis and improve OS in high-risk nmCRPC. With PSMA-PET, most such patients would now be reclassified as metastatic.

trials.name: EMBARK
trials.takeaway: Combined enzalutamide + ADT for high-risk BCR.

inclusion: High-risk biochemical recurrence with PSADT ≤9 months
strengths: Enzalutamide monotherapy arm offered testosterone-sparing option
appraisal.critique: Enzalutamide with ADT improves metastasis-free survival in high-risk biochemical recurrence. OS data and PSMA-PET staging will shape its use.

trials.name: TAX 327
trials.takeaway: First chemotherapy with survival benefit in mCRPC.

appraisal.critique: Docetaxel was the first chemotherapy to prolong survival in mCRPC. The 3-weekly schedule became standard.

trials.name: COU-AA-301/302, AFFIRM, PREVAIL
trials.result: AFFIRM mOS 18.4 vs 13.6 mo; PREVAIL OS HR 0.71
trials.takeaway: ARPIs prolong survival in mCRPC.

appraisal.critique: Abiraterone and enzalutamide improve OS in mCRPC before and after docetaxel. Cross-resistance means switching ARPIs is less effective.

trials.name: TROPIC / CARD
trials.population: mCRPC after docetaxel (and an ARPI in CARD)
trials.takeaway: Cabazitaxel preferred over a second ARPI after docetaxel + ARPI.

inclusion: mCRPC after docetaxel (and an ARPI in CARD)
strengths: CARD showed superiority over ARPI switch
appraisal.critique: Cabazitaxel improves OS after docetaxel and is better than switching ARPI (CARD). Neutropenia requires G-CSF prophylaxis.

trials.name: ALSYMPCA
trials.population: Symptomatic bone-metastatic CRPC, no visceral mets
trials.takeaway: Radium-223 for bone-predominant mCRPC (not with abiraterone).

appraisal.critique: Radium-223 improves OS in bone-only mCRPC. Combination with abiraterone increased fractures (ERA 223), so bone health agents are recommended.

trials.name: VISION
trials.population: PSMA-PET+ mCRPC after ARPI and taxane
trials.takeaway: Lu-PSMA is standard after ARPI and taxane in PSMA+ mCRPC.

limitations: Open-label with early dropout in control
appraisal.critique: Lu-PSMA improves OS in heavily pretreated mCRPC. The control arm excluded chemotherapy and had early dropouts, which may favour Lu-PSMA.

trials.name: PSMAfore
trials.population: Taxane-naive PSMA+ mCRPC after one ARPI
trials.takeaway: Lu-PSMA can be used before chemotherapy.

inclusion: Taxane-naive PSMA+ mCRPC after one ARPI
appraisal.critique: Lu-PSMA before docetaxel improves rPFS, but OS is confounded by crossover. It is an option for patients unfit or unwilling for chemotherapy.

trials.name: PROfound
trials.population: mCRPC with HRR alterations after ARPI
trials.result: Cohort A rPFS 7.4 vs 3.6 mo; OS 19.1 vs 14.7 mo
trials.takeaway: Test HRR genes; PARP inhibitor for BRCA-altered mCRPC.

inclusion: mCRPC with HRR alterations after ARPI
strengths: OS benefit in BRCA1/2, ATM cohort
appraisal.critique: Olaparib improves OS in mCRPC with BRCA1/2 or ATM alterations. Benefit in other HRR genes is uncertain, and the control arm was ARPI switch.

trials.name: TALAPRO-2 / PROpel
trials.result: Greatest benefit in BRCA-mutated; TALAPRO-2 OS benefit reported
trials.takeaway: PARPi + ARPI first line, especially for HRR/BRCA-altered disease.

appraisal.critique: PARPi + ARPI improves rPFS in first-line mCRPC, mainly in HRR-mutated patients. Use in HRR-negative patients is debated.

trials.name: SWOG 8710
trials.takeaway: Cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemo before cystectomy.

appraisal.critique: Established neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy for MIBC, improving survival. Toxicity and slow accrual reflect the challenges of neoadjuvant therapy.

trials.name: VESPER
trials.takeaway: ddMVAC is a preferred neoadjuvant regimen.

appraisal.critique: Dose-dense MVAC gives better PFS than gem-cis. Toxicity is higher, so patient selection matters.

trials.name: NIAGARA
trials.takeaway: Perioperative durvalumab is a new standard for MIBC.

appraisal.critique: Perioperative durvalumab with gem-cis improves EFS and OS in cisplatin-eligible MIBC. Because durvalumab was given both before and after surgery, the contribution of each phase cannot be separated, and only cisplatin-eligible patients were studied.

trials.name: CheckMate 274
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab for high-risk resected urothelial cancer.

inclusion: With or without prior neoadjuvant chemo
appraisal.critique: Adjuvant nivolumab improves DFS in high-risk MIUC after surgery. OS data are immature, and the benefit in upper-tract tumours and PD-L1-negative disease is less certain.

trials.name: BC2001
trials.takeaway: Trimodality bladder preservation with concurrent 5-FU/MMC is standard.

appraisal.critique: Chemoradiotherapy with 5-FU/MMC improves locoregional control for bladder preservation. OS was not improved, but bladder preservation is a key quality-of-life benefit.

trials.name: POUT
trials.population: Upper-tract urothelial carcinoma pT2–T4 or N+
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant platinum chemo after nephroureterectomy.

inclusion: Upper-tract urothelial carcinoma pT2–T4 or N+
limitations: Carboplatin used if renal function poor
appraisal.critique: Adjuvant chemotherapy improves DFS in UTUC. Carboplatin was used for patients with poor renal function.

trials.name: JAVELIN Bladder 100
trials.population: Advanced UC without progression after first-line platinum
trials.takeaway: Switch-maintenance avelumab after platinum response.

inclusion: Advanced UC without progression after first-line platinum
appraisal.critique: Avelumab maintenance improves OS after platinum. Its role has diminished with EV-pembro first-line.

trials.name: EV-302
trials.result: mOS 31.5 vs 16.1 mo (HR 0.47); mPFS 12.5 vs 6.3 mo
trials.takeaway: EV + pembrolizumab replaced platinum chemo first line.

appraisal.critique: EV-pembro roughly doubles OS over platinum chemotherapy in first-line advanced urothelial cancer — a landmark shift. Rash, neuropathy and hyperglycaemia require monitoring, and cost is a major barrier in India.

trials.name: CheckMate 901 (gem-cis + nivo)
trials.takeaway: Alternative first-line regimen when EV not available.

appraisal.critique: Nivolumab with gem-cis improves OS in cisplatin-eligible advanced UC. EV-pembro is now preferred.

trials.name: THOR
trials.takeaway: Test FGFR3; erdafitinib for altered tumours.

appraisal.critique: Erdafitinib improves OS in FGFR-altered UC after prior therapy, supporting routine FGFR testing. Hyperphosphataemia, nail and ocular toxicity need monitoring.

trials.name: CheckMate 214
trials.result: Int/poor-risk: mOS 47.0 vs 26.6 mo (HR 0.68); durable CR ~10%
trials.takeaway: Nivo-ipi first line for intermediate/poor-risk ccRCC.

strengths: Durable OS benefit in intermediate/poor risk
appraisal.critique: Nivo-ipi gives durable long-term OS benefit in intermediate/poor-risk ccRCC, with a plateau of long-term responders. In favourable-risk disease, sunitinib did as well, and immune toxicity needs experienced management.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-426 / CLEAR / CheckMate 9ER
trials.result: CLEAR mPFS 23.9 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.39); all showed OS benefit
trials.takeaway: IO-TKI combinations are first-line standards across risk groups.

appraisal.critique: IO-TKI combinations improve OS over sunitinib in advanced ccRCC and achieve high response rates. TKI toxicity requires dose management, and long-term durability vs nivo-ipi is still debated.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-564
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant pembrolizumab for intermediate-high/high-risk resected ccRCC.

appraisal.critique: Adjuvant pembrolizumab improves DFS and OS in high-risk ccRCC after nephrectomy. Many patients are cured by surgery alone and are exposed to immune toxicity without benefit.

trials.name: CARMENA
trials.takeaway: Upfront cytoreductive nephrectomy is not routine for intermediate/poor-risk mRCC.

appraisal.critique: Showed sunitinib alone is non-inferior to cytoreductive nephrectomy followed by sunitinib in intermediate/poor-risk mRCC. Poor accrual and a high-risk population limit applicability to the IO era.

trials.name: LITESPARK-005
trials.population: Advanced ccRCC after IO and VEGF-TKI
trials.takeaway: HIF-2α inhibitor option in later-line ccRCC.

inclusion: Advanced ccRCC after IO and VEGF-TKI
appraisal.critique: Belzutifan improves PFS in advanced ccRCC after IO and VEGF-TKI. OS was not improved.

trials.name: Einhorn PVB / BEP (Williams)
trials.result: Equal efficacy with less neuromuscular toxicity with etoposide
trials.takeaway: BEP is the cornerstone; cisplatin made metastatic GCT curable.

appraisal.critique: BEP replaced PVB with less neuromuscular toxicity and equivalent efficacy. It remains the standard for germ cell tumours.

trials.name: IGCCCG
trials.takeaway: Risk group guides BEP ×3 vs ×4 (or VIP).

appraisal.critique: Defined prognostic groups that guide risk-adapted therapy. It remains the basis for treatment decisions.

trials.name: MRC TE19 (Oliver)
trials.result: 5-y RFS 94.7% vs 96.0% (non-inferior); fewer contralateral GCTs with carboplatin
trials.takeaway: Surveillance or one cycle carboplatin; adjuvant RT largely abandoned.

appraisal.critique: Single-dose carboplatin is non-inferior to RT for stage I seminoma. Surveillance is now preferred for low-risk patients.

trials.name: GOG 111 / OV-10
trials.takeaway: Platinum-taxane became first-line standard (carboplatin later per GOG 158).

inclusion: Stage III–IV ovarian cancer after surgery
appraisal.critique: Established platinum-paclitaxel as the standard first-line chemotherapy for advanced ovarian cancer. Carboplatin later replaced cisplatin with similar efficacy and less toxicity (GOG 158).

trials.name: GOG 172 (Armstrong IP)
trials.population: Optimally debulked stage III ovarian cancer
trials.result: mOS 65.6 vs 49.7 mo; only 42% completed IP therapy
trials.takeaway: IP chemo improves OS but is toxic; GOG 252 later showed no benefit with modern regimens.

inclusion: Optimally debulked (≤1 cm) stage III ovarian cancer
appraisal.critique: IP chemotherapy improves OS but is rarely used due to toxicity and complexity; GOG 252 did not confirm benefit with modified regimens.

trials.name: JGOG 3016
trials.result: mOS 100.5 vs 62.2 mo in Japanese population; not replicated in ICON8
trials.takeaway: Weekly paclitaxel is an option; benefit population-dependent.

appraisal.critique: Dose-dense weekly paclitaxel improved OS in Japanese patients, but ICON8 and GOG 262 did not confirm benefit in Western populations. It remains an option, especially where 3-weekly regimens are poorly tolerated.

trials.name: EORTC 55971 / CHORUS
trials.result: Equivalent OS; lower surgical morbidity with NACT
trials.takeaway: Neoadjuvant chemo is appropriate when complete primary cytoreduction is unlikely.

appraisal.critique: NACT followed by interval debulking is non-inferior to primary surgery for stage IIIC–IV ovarian cancer, with less morbidity. Low complete resection rates in primary surgery arms have been criticised; TRUST may refine this.

trials.name: OVHIPEC-1
trials.population: Stage III ovarian cancer after NACT
trials.takeaway: HIPEC at interval debulking is an option.

inclusion: Stage III ovarian cancer after 3 cycles NACT
appraisal.critique: HIPEC at interval debulking improved OS and RFS. The trial was open-label and small, and HIPEC requires expertise, so it is not universally adopted.

trials.name: SOLO-1
trials.population: BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian cancer responding to platinum
trials.takeaway: Olaparib maintenance for BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer.

inclusion: BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian cancer responding to platinum
appraisal.critique: Olaparib maintenance gives a large, durable PFS and OS benefit in BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer, with many patients long-term disease-free. It makes BRCA testing at diagnosis mandatory.

trials.name: PAOLA-1
trials.population: Advanced ovarian cancer after platinum + bevacizumab
trials.takeaway: Olaparib + bevacizumab maintenance for HRD-positive disease.

inclusion: Advanced ovarian cancer after platinum + bevacizumab
strengths: PFS and OS benefit in HRD-positive
appraisal.critique: Olaparib with bevacizumab improves PFS and OS in HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer. Little benefit in HRD-negative tumours means HRD testing is needed.

trials.name: PRIMA
trials.population: Advanced ovarian cancer responding to first-line platinum
trials.result: Overall PFS 13.8 vs 8.2 mo (HR 0.62); HRD 21.9 vs 10.4 mo; no OS benefit
trials.takeaway: Niraparib maintenance regardless of biomarker (benefit largest in HRD).

inclusion: Advanced ovarian cancer responding to first-line platinum
appraisal.critique: Niraparib improves PFS in advanced ovarian cancer across biomarker groups, but final OS showed no benefit. Thrombocytopenia requires weight-based dosing.

trials.name: ICON7 / GOG 218
trials.result: Modest PFS benefit; OS gain in high-risk subgroup (ICON7)
trials.takeaway: Bevacizumab for high-risk / suboptimally debulked disease.

limitations: OS benefit only in high-risk subgroup
appraisal.critique: Bevacizumab improves PFS in advanced ovarian cancer, with OS benefit only in high-risk subgroups. Cost and hypertension limit use in India.

trials.name: MIRASOL
trials.takeaway: Test FRα; mirvetuximab for FRα-high platinum-resistant disease.

appraisal.critique: Mirvetuximab improves OS in FRα-high platinum-resistant ovarian cancer — a rare positive trial in this setting. Ocular toxicity (keratopathy, blurred vision) requires eye care.

trials.name: PORTEC-1/2
trials.result: Vaginal recurrence 1.8% vs 1.6%; less GI toxicity with VBT
trials.takeaway: Vaginal brachytherapy replaces pelvic RT for high-intermediate risk.

appraisal.critique: Vaginal brachytherapy gives similar vaginal control to pelvic EBRT with less toxicity in high-intermediate-risk endometrial cancer. Molecular classification (PORTEC-4a) now refines who needs any RT.

trials.name: PORTEC-3
trials.result: 5-y OS 81.4% vs 76.1%; largest benefit in stage III and p53-abnormal
trials.takeaway: ChemoRT for high-risk disease, especially p53-abnormal.

strengths: Benefit in serous and stage III
appraisal.critique: ChemoRT improves OS in high-risk endometrial cancer, especially serous histology and stage III. Long-term neuropathy and toxicity are significant, and molecular subgroup analysis shows p53-abnormal tumours benefit most.

trials.name: GOG 258
trials.result: No RFS difference; fewer vaginal/nodal recurrences with RT
trials.takeaway: Chemotherapy alone is reasonable for stage III; RT improves local control.

appraisal.critique: ChemoRT did not improve RFS over chemotherapy alone in stage III–IVA endometrial cancer, but reduced pelvic and vaginal recurrence. Combined with PORTEC-3, it supports chemotherapy as the backbone with selective RT.

trials.name: RUBY / NRG-GY018
trials.population: Stage III–IV or recurrent endometrial cancer
trials.result: dMMR: PFS HR 0.28–0.30; RUBY OS benefit overall
trials.takeaway: Chemo-IO first line, profound benefit in dMMR.

inclusion: Stage III–IV or recurrent endometrial cancer
appraisal.critique: Adding dostarlimab or pembrolizumab to carboplatin-paclitaxel improves PFS, with the largest benefit in dMMR tumours. In pMMR disease the gain is modest.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-775
trials.takeaway: Len-pembro for pMMR endometrial cancer after platinum.

appraisal.critique: Lenvatinib-pembrolizumab improves OS after platinum in advanced endometrial cancer, including pMMR tumours. Toxicity (hypertension, fatigue, hypothyroidism) often needs dose reductions.

trials.name: Cervix chemoRT (Rose / Morris, 1999 NCI alert)
trials.takeaway: Weekly cisplatin + EBRT + brachytherapy is standard.

appraisal.critique: Cisplatin-based chemoRT improves OS in locally advanced cervical cancer and is the global standard. Older RT techniques without image-guided brachytherapy were used, which modern practice has improved.

trials.name: EMBRACE-I
trials.takeaway: Image-guided adaptive brachytherapy with dose targets (HR-CTV D90 ≥85 Gy) is standard.

appraisal.critique: MRI-guided adaptive brachytherapy gives excellent local control with low morbidity. It is non-randomised but large; access to MRI-based brachytherapy is limited in India.

trials.name: INTERLACE
trials.population: Stage IB1 N+ to IVA cervical cancer
trials.takeaway: Short induction chemo before chemoRT is a new standard option.

inclusion: Stage IB1 N+ to IVA cervical cancer
appraisal.critique: Six weeks of weekly carboplatin-paclitaxel before chemoRT improves OS in locally advanced cervical cancer. It is cheap and practical, though few stage III–IVA patients were included and it pre-dates IO.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-A18
trials.population: High-risk LACC (FIGO 2014 IB2–IIB N+ or III–IVA)
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab with chemoRT for high-risk LACC.

appraisal.critique: Pembrolizumab with chemoRT improves PFS and OS in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer. Cost is a major barrier in India, where cervical cancer burden is high.

trials.name: GOG 240
trials.takeaway: Bevacizumab added to first-line chemo.

appraisal.critique: Adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy improves OS in recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer. Fistula risk, especially after pelvic RT, requires caution.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-826
trials.takeaway: Chemo-IO ± bevacizumab is first-line standard for PD-L1+ disease.

appraisal.critique: Pembrolizumab with chemotherapy ± bevacizumab improves OS in persistent/recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer. Benefit is mainly in PD-L1 CPS ≥1, which is most patients.

trials.name: SHAPE
trials.result: 3-y pelvic recurrence 2.5% vs 2.2% (non-inferior); less urinary dysfunction
trials.takeaway: Simple hysterectomy is adequate for low-risk early cervical cancer.

appraisal.critique: Simple hysterectomy is non-inferior to radical hysterectomy for low-risk early cervical cancer, with less urinary morbidity. Careful pre-operative imaging and selection are essential.

trials.name: LACC
trials.takeaway: Open surgery is preferred for radical hysterectomy.

appraisal.critique: Minimally invasive radical hysterectomy had worse DFS and OS than open surgery for early cervical cancer, reversing practice. Surgeon experience and uterine manipulator use have been debated.

trials.name: MACH-NC
trials.takeaway: Concurrent platinum chemoRT is the reference for locally advanced HNSCC.

inclusion: Randomised trials adding chemotherapy to locoregional treatment of non-metastatic HNSCC
strengths: Showed timing matters: concurrent chemo gives ~6.5% 5-year OS gain
limitations: Benefit declines with age; little or none >70 years
appraisal.critique: Basis for concurrent chemoRT in HNSCC. The age interaction is important — elderly patients get little benefit and more toxicity.

trials.name: MARCH
trials.takeaway: Altered fractionation helps when RT is given alone.

inclusion: Randomised trials of altered fractionation vs conventional RT in HNSCC
exclusion: Trials with concurrent chemotherapy in both arms
strengths: Showed hyperfractionation gives the largest OS benefit (~8% at 5 years)
limitations: Mostly RT-alone comparisons, pre-dating concurrent chemoRT
appraisal.critique: Altered fractionation is an alternative when chemotherapy is not possible; with concurrent chemotherapy its added value is limited.

trials.name: RTOG 9501 / EORTC 22931
trials.result: Pooled: benefit confined to positive margins and/or extranodal extension
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant chemoRT for positive margins or ENE.

inclusion: Resected HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, hypopharynx)
High-risk features: positive margins, extracapsular extension, ≥2 nodes (RTOG), or other adverse features (EORTC)
exclusion: Prior RT to head and neck
strengths: Pooled analysis identified margins and ECE as key indications
limitations: OS benefit in RTOG trial not significant in long-term follow-up overall
appraisal.critique: Postoperative chemoRT is standard for positive margins and ECE. Other risk factors gain less from chemotherapy.

trials.name: Bonner cetuximab-RT
trials.takeaway: Cetuximab-RT improves on RT alone, but is inferior to cisplatin (see RTOG 1016).

inclusion: Stage III–IV non-metastatic HNSCC of oropharynx, larynx or hypopharynx
strengths: Less mucositis than expected with cetuximab
limitations: Compared with RT alone, not chemoRT
appraisal.critique: Cetuximab-RT is inferior to cisplatin-RT (RTOG 1016, De-ESCALaTE) and is now reserved for cisplatin-ineligible patients, where even its role is questioned.

trials.name: RTOG 1016 / De-ESCALaTE
trials.takeaway: Cisplatin remains standard even in HPV+ disease; cetuximab is not a de-escalation.

inclusion: T1–T2 N2a–N3 or T3–T4 N0–N3 (RTOG 1016); low-risk (De-ESCALaTE)
appraisal.critique: Cisplatin remains standard for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. Cetuximab de-escalation failed; other de-escalation strategies are under study.

trials.name: Noronha (Tata) weekly vs 3-weekly cisplatin
trials.takeaway: 3-weekly high-dose cisplatin preferred in the postoperative setting.

inclusion: Locally advanced HNSCC treated with chemoRT
limitations: Weekly dose 30 mg/m² lower than many use (40 mg/m²)
appraisal.critique: Supports 3-weekly cisplatin in the postoperative setting. Many argue weekly 40 mg/m² (as in JCOG1008) is a fairer comparison.

trials.name: JCOG1008
trials.takeaway: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² is an acceptable postoperative alternative.

inclusion: Postoperative high-risk HNSCC (positive margins or ECE)
limitations: Locoregional control slightly worse in weekly arm
appraisal.critique: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² is non-inferior to 3-weekly 100 mg/m² in the postoperative high-risk setting, with less toxicity. Together with Noronha's trial, the choice depends on setting and patient fitness.

trials.name: PARSPORT
trials.takeaway: IMRT is standard to reduce xerostomia.

strengths: Randomised evidence that parotid-sparing IMRT reduces xerostomia
appraisal.critique: Parotid-sparing IMRT reduces xerostomia and improves quality of life over conventional RT. It made IMRT the standard for head and neck RT.

trials.name: VA Larynx / RTOG 91-11
trials.result: Concurrent chemoRT gave highest larynx preservation (~84% at 2 y)
trials.takeaway: Organ preservation with concurrent chemoRT for suitable T3/low-volume T4 larynx.

inclusion: Stage III–IV laryngeal SCC requiring total laryngectomy
limitations: Late deaths unrelated to cancer higher in concurrent arm (RTOG 91-11)
appraisal.critique: Concurrent cisplatin-RT gives the best larynx preservation, but late toxicity and non-cancer deaths are concerns.

trials.name: TAX 324 / TAX 323
trials.takeaway: If induction is used, TPF is the regimen; routine induction not proven over chemoRT.

inclusion: Locally advanced unresectable HNSCC (TAX 323) or resectable/unresectable (TAX 324)
strengths: Showed TPF superior to PF induction
limitations: Did not compare induction with concurrent chemoRT alone
appraisal.critique: TPF is the preferred induction regimen, but induction itself has not shown OS benefit over chemoRT in most trials.

trials.name: Sun / Zhang NPC GP induction
trials.result: Zhang: 3-y RFS 85.3% vs 76.5%; OS benefit later
trials.takeaway: GP induction + chemoRT is standard for locally advanced NPC.

appraisal.critique: GP induction before chemoRT improves OS in locoregionally advanced NPC. It comes from endemic EBV-related NPC in China; applicability to non-endemic populations is assumed.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-048
trials.result: CPS ≥20 pembro alone mOS 14.9 vs 10.7 mo; chemo-pembro OS benefit overall
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab (± chemo) replaced EXTREME first line.

inclusion: Recurrent or metastatic HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, larynx)
exclusion: Progression within 6 months of curative treatment
limitations: Pembrolizumab monotherapy not beneficial in CPS <1
appraisal.critique: Pembrolizumab ± chemotherapy improves OS over EXTREME in first-line R/M HNSCC. Monotherapy is not effective in CPS <1, so CPS guides choice.

trials.name: CheckMate 141
trials.takeaway: Nivolumab for platinum-refractory HNSCC.

appraisal.critique: Nivolumab improves OS over investigator's choice in platinum-refractory R/M HNSCC, with better quality of life. Response rates are low (~13%), but responses are durable.

trials.name: Patil (Tata) metronomic
arms: Oral metronomic methotrexate + celecoxib ± low-dose nivolumab
trials.result: Low-dose nivolumab 40 mg + metronomic: 1-y OS 43.4% vs 16.3%
trials.takeaway: Affordable options for LMIC settings.

limitations: Low-dose nivolumab not compared with full dose
appraisal.critique: Low-dose nivolumab (40 mg) with metronomic chemotherapy improved OS in R/M HNSCC — a low-cost, practical option for India. It was single-centre and did not compare low dose with standard dose.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-689
arms: Neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab with standard therapy
trials.takeaway: Perioperative pembrolizumab for resectable PD-L1+ HNSCC.

inclusion: Resectable stage III–IVA HNSCC (oral cavity, larynx, hypopharynx, HPV-negative oropharynx)
appraisal.critique: Perioperative pembrolizumab improves EFS in resectable locally advanced HNSCC, with benefit mainly in PD-L1-positive tumours. OS data are immature.

trials.name: EORTC/NCIC (Stupp)
arms: RT 60 Gy/30 + concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide
trials.result: mOS 14.6 vs 12.1 mo; 5-y OS 9.8% vs 1.9%; MGMT methylation predicts benefit
trials.takeaway: Stupp protocol is standard for GBM.

appraisal.critique: TMZ with RT improved OS in newly diagnosed GBM, especially in MGMT-methylated tumours. Patients over 70 were excluded, and the benefit in unmethylated tumours is small.

trials.name: Perry elderly GBM
trials.result: mOS 9.3 vs 7.6 mo; MGMT-methylated 13.5 vs 7.7 mo
trials.takeaway: Hypofractionated RT + TMZ for older patients.

strengths: OS benefit with TMZ in elderly
appraisal.critique: Adding TMZ to short-course RT improves OS in elderly GBM, especially MGMT-methylated tumours. It is a practical, tolerable regimen for older patients.

trials.name: EF-14 (TTFields)
trials.takeaway: Tumour-treating fields are an option with maintenance TMZ.

appraisal.critique: TTFields with TMZ improved OS in GBM after chemoRT. The open-label design without sham control, device burden and cost limit adoption.

trials.name: RTOG 9802 / EORTC 22033
trials.takeaway: RT + PCV for high-risk LGG (IDH-mutant).

inclusion: High-risk low-grade glioma (age ≥40 or subtotal resection)
appraisal.critique: RT with PCV improves OS in high-risk low-grade glioma. Molecular analysis shows benefit is greatest in IDH-mutant tumours.

trials.name: RTOG 9402 / EORTC 26951
trials.takeaway: RT + PCV for 1p/19q co-deleted oligodendroglioma.

appraisal.critique: RT with PCV improves OS in 1p/19q-codeleted anaplastic oligodendroglioma. It defined molecular markers as predictive in glioma.

trials.name: CATNON
trials.result: Adjuvant TMZ improved OS (HR 0.64), benefit in IDH-mutant
trials.takeaway: RT + 12 cycles adjuvant TMZ for IDH-mutant grade 3 astrocytoma.

appraisal.critique: Adjuvant TMZ improves OS in 1p/19q non-codeleted anaplastic glioma, mainly in IDH-mutant tumours. Concurrent TMZ added no benefit.

trials.name: INDIGO
trials.population: Residual/recurrent grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma after surgery only
trials.takeaway: Vorasidenib can delay RT/chemo in grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma.

inclusion: Residual or recurrent grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma after surgery only
strengths: PFS benefit and delayed need for further therapy
appraisal.critique: Vorasidenib improves PFS and delays the need for RT or chemotherapy in grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma. OS and long-term neurocognitive benefits are not yet shown.

trials.name: Patchell (surgery + WBRT)
trials.takeaway: Resection for single accessible metastasis.

appraisal.critique: Surgery plus WBRT improves OS and functional independence for a single brain metastasis. It pre-dates SRS, which is now an alternative.

trials.name: N0574 (Brown)
trials.result: Cognitive decline at 3 mo 63.5% vs 91.7%; no OS difference
trials.takeaway: SRS alone is preferred for limited brain metastases.

strengths: Less cognitive decline with SRS alone
appraisal.critique: SRS alone causes less cognitive decline than SRS + WBRT for 1–3 brain metastases, with similar OS. Higher intracranial recurrence without WBRT requires MRI surveillance.

trials.name: JLGK0901 (Yamamoto)
trials.result: OS for 5–10 lesions non-inferior to 2–4 lesions
trials.takeaway: SRS is reasonable for up to 10 metastases.

appraisal.critique: SRS alone for 5–10 metastases gives non-inferior OS compared with 2–4 metastases. It is observational, so it supports but does not prove SRS for multiple metastases.

trials.name: NRG CC001
trials.takeaway: If WBRT is needed, use hippocampal avoidance + memantine.

strengths: Less cognitive decline with hippocampal avoidance
appraisal.critique: Hippocampal-avoidance WBRT with memantine reduces cognitive decline compared with WBRT + memantine. It requires IMRT and careful planning.

trials.name: QUARTZ
trials.population: NSCLC brain mets unsuitable for surgery/SRS
trials.result: No meaningful difference in QALYs or OS
trials.takeaway: WBRT adds little for poor-prognosis patients.

inclusion: NSCLC brain metastases unsuitable for surgery/SRS
strengths: Showed no OS benefit from WBRT
appraisal.critique: WBRT did not improve OS or quality of life in poor-prognosis NSCLC brain metastases. Supportive care alone is appropriate for these patients.

trials.name: IFM 2009
trials.result: mPFS 50 vs 36 mo; no OS difference
trials.takeaway: Early ASCT improves PFS; still standard for eligible patients.

appraisal.critique: Early ASCT after RVD improves PFS but not OS compared with RVD alone and ASCT at relapse. Deferring ASCT is an option for selected patients.

trials.name: GRIFFIN / PERSEUS
arms: D-VRd induction + ASCT + D-VRd consolidation + D-R maintenance
trials.result: PERSEUS 4-y PFS 84.3% vs 67.7% (HR 0.42); MRD negativity 75% vs 48%
trials.takeaway: Quadruplet D-VRd is the standard for transplant-eligible myeloma.

appraisal.critique: Adding daratumumab to VRd induction, ASCT and maintenance improves PFS and MRD negativity. D-VRd is the new standard for transplant-eligible myeloma.

trials.name: MAIA
trials.takeaway: DRd is a standard for transplant-ineligible myeloma.

appraisal.critique: Daratumumab with Rd improves PFS and OS in transplant-ineligible myeloma. Continuous therapy and infection risk require monitoring.

trials.name: CEPHEUS / IMROZ
trials.takeaway: Quadruplets also benefit fit transplant-ineligible patients.

appraisal.critique: Quadruplet therapy (anti-CD38 + VRd) improves PFS in transplant-ineligible or deferred myeloma. Toxicity in frail elderly patients requires careful selection.

trials.name: CALGB 100104 / Myeloma XI
trials.takeaway: Lenalidomide maintenance until progression after ASCT.

appraisal.critique: Lenalidomide maintenance after ASCT improves OS. Second primary malignancies are a known risk.

trials.name: CARTITUDE-4
trials.takeaway: BCMA CAR-T moves to second line.

appraisal.critique: Cilta-cel improves PFS and OS in lenalidomide-refractory myeloma after 1–3 lines. Early deaths, CRS and neurotoxicity, and limited access are concerns.

trials.name: MajesTEC-3
trials.takeaway: Bispecific + anti-CD38 is a powerful early-relapse option.

appraisal.critique: Teclistamab with daratumumab improves PFS and OS in relapsed myeloma. Infection risk requires prophylaxis and IVIG.

trials.name: GELA LNH98-5 (R-CHOP)
trials.takeaway: R-CHOP became the DLBCL standard.

appraisal.critique: R-CHOP improved OS over CHOP in elderly DLBCL and became the global standard. Rituximab biosimilars have improved access in India.

trials.name: POLARIX
trials.takeaway: Pola-R-CHP is an alternative first line for higher-IPI DLBCL.

appraisal.critique: Pola-R-CHP improves PFS over R-CHOP in intermediate/high-risk DLBCL, but not OS. Cost limits uptake.

trials.name: ZUMA-7 / TRANSFORM
trials.population: Primary refractory or early relapse (<12 mo) LBCL
trials.result: ZUMA-7 mEFS 8.3 vs 2.0 mo; OS HR 0.73
trials.takeaway: CAR-T is standard second line for early relapse.

inclusion: Primary refractory or early relapse LBCL
appraisal.critique: CAR-T improves EFS and OS over salvage chemotherapy and ASCT in early relapsed LBCL. Access, cost and toxicity limit use in India.

trials.name: HD10 / HD16 / RAPID
trials.result: HD10: ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy as effective as ×4 + 30 Gy; PET-neg RT omission slightly ↑ relapse
trials.takeaway: Brief chemo + low-dose RT; RT omission trades small relapse increase for less late toxicity.

appraisal.critique: PET-guided RT omission in early favourable HL slightly increases relapse but avoids RT late effects. Shared decisions based on age and RT field are key.

trials.name: RATHL
trials.takeaway: Omit bleomycin after negative interim PET.

appraisal.critique: Dropping bleomycin after negative interim PET reduces lung toxicity without compromising efficacy in advanced HL. PET-positive patients still do poorly.

trials.name: ECHELON-1
trials.takeaway: BV-AVD is a first-line option for advanced HL.

appraisal.critique: A-AVD improves OS over ABVD in stage III–IV HL. Neuropathy and febrile neutropenia require G-CSF.

trials.name: HD21
trials.takeaway: BrECADD is a new standard in advanced HL (where available).

appraisal.critique: BrECADD improves PFS with less toxicity than eBEACOPP in advanced HL. It is suitable for fit younger patients.

trials.name: S1826
trials.takeaway: N-AVD is emerging as a first-line standard for advanced HL, including adolescents.

appraisal.critique: Nivolumab-AVD improves PFS over brentuximab-AVD in advanced HL. OS data are awaited.

trials.name: PRIMA (FL)
trials.takeaway: Rituximab maintenance prolongs PFS in FL.

appraisal.critique: Rituximab maintenance improves PFS in advanced FL but not OS. Infection risk and cost must be considered.

trials.name: StiL / BRIGHT
trials.result: StiL mPFS 69.5 vs 31.2 mo with less toxicity
trials.takeaway: BR is a standard first-line option for indolent lymphoma.

appraisal.critique: BR improves PFS with less toxicity than R-CHOP in indolent NHL and MCL. Prolonged lymphopenia increases infection risk.

trials.name: TRIANGLE
trials.result: Ibrutinib without ASCT non-inferior/superior to ASCT
trials.takeaway: BTK inhibitor added to induction; ASCT may be omitted.

strengths: Showed ASCT may be omitted with ibrutinib
appraisal.critique: Adding ibrutinib to induction and maintenance allows ASCT omission in younger fit MCL. OS data are awaited.

trials.name: CLL14 / ELEVATE-TN / RESONATE-2
trials.takeaway: Targeted therapy (BTKi or Ven-O) has replaced chemoimmunotherapy.

appraisal.critique: Targeted agents improve PFS over chemoimmunotherapy in untreated CLL. Choice between continuous BTKi and fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab depends on comorbidities and preference.

trials.name: Daunorubicin 90 vs 45 (E1900)
trials.takeaway: 7+3 with daunorubicin 60–90 mg/m² is standard induction.

appraisal.critique: Daunorubicin 90 mg/m² improves OS over 45 mg/m² in younger AML. NCRI AML17 suggested 60 mg/m² is equivalent to 90 mg/m².

trials.name: RATIFY
trials.takeaway: Test FLT3 at diagnosis; add midostaurin (or quizartinib).

appraisal.critique: Midostaurin with 7+3 improves OS in FLT3-mutated AML. Many patients proceeded to transplant, which may have contributed.

trials.name: VIALE-A
trials.takeaway: Ven-Aza is standard for unfit AML.

appraisal.critique: Venetoclax with azacitidine improves OS in AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy. Myelosuppression and infection require monitoring.

trials.name: APL0406 (Lo-Coco)
trials.takeaway: ATRA-ATO without chemo for non-high-risk APL.

appraisal.critique: ATRA + ATO improves EFS over ATRA + chemotherapy in low/intermediate-risk APL. It is a chemotherapy-free cure for most patients.

trials.name: IRIS
trials.takeaway: TKIs transformed CML into a chronic disease.

appraisal.critique: Imatinib transformed CML into a chronic disease with near-normal life expectancy. Generic imatinib is widely available in India.

trials.name: PhALLCON / GIMEMA LAL2116
trials.result: D-ALBA: molecular response 60% after blinatumomab; 3-y OS ~80%
trials.takeaway: Chemo-light TKI + blinatumomab approaches for Ph+ ALL.

appraisal.critique: Ponatinib and chemo-free regimens achieve high MRD negativity in Ph+ ALL. Long-term outcomes are awaited.

trials.name: E1910
trials.takeaway: Blinatumomab in consolidation even when MRD-negative.

appraisal.critique: Blinatumomab consolidation improves OS in MRD-negative B-ALL. Neurotoxicity and cost are concerns.

trials.name: CheckMate 067
trials.result: 10-y OS 43% (combo) vs 37% vs 19%; mOS 71.9 mo with combo
trials.takeaway: Combination checkpoint blockade gives durable long-term survival.

limitations: Not powered for combo vs nivo
appraisal.critique: Nivo-ipi gives the longest OS in advanced melanoma, with ~50% alive at 10 years. Grade 3–4 toxicity in ~60% requires experienced management.

trials.name: RELATIVITY-047
trials.takeaway: LAG-3 + PD-1 is a less toxic first-line combination.

appraisal.critique: Nivolumab-relatlimab improves PFS over nivolumab alone with less toxicity than nivo-ipi. OS was not significantly improved.

trials.name: COMBI-d/v & COLUMBUS
trials.takeaway: BRAF/MEK combination for BRAF-mutant melanoma.

strengths: Less skin toxicity than BRAFi alone
appraisal.critique: BRAF/MEK combinations improve OS over BRAFi alone in BRAF V600 melanoma. Resistance develops, so durability is less than IO.

trials.name: DREAMseq
trials.takeaway: Start with immunotherapy even in BRAF-mutant melanoma.

appraisal.critique: Starting with nivo-ipi gives better OS than starting with BRAF/MEK in BRAF V600 melanoma. Immunotherapy first is preferred.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-054 / CheckMate 238 / COMBI-AD
trials.result: Pembro RFS HR 0.57; COMBI-AD OS HR 0.57 at first analysis
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant anti-PD-1 or BRAF/MEK for resected stage III.

appraisal.critique: Adjuvant therapy improves RFS in resected stage III melanoma. OS benefit is not proven.

trials.name: SWOG S1801
trials.takeaway: Neoadjuvant IO before surgery for macroscopic stage III.

appraisal.critique: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab improves EFS over adjuvant pembrolizumab alone. Neoadjuvant IO is now preferred for resectable melanoma.

trials.name: NADINA
trials.takeaway: Neoadjuvant ipi-nivo is a new standard.

appraisal.critique: Neoadjuvant nivo-ipi with response-adapted surgery improves EFS over upfront surgery and adjuvant nivolumab. It is a new standard.

trials.name: MSLT-II / DeCOG-SLT
trials.takeaway: Completion dissection no longer routine after positive SLNB.

strengths: Showed no OS benefit for completion dissection
appraisal.critique: Completion lymph node dissection does not improve OS in sentinel node-positive melanoma. Ultrasound surveillance is standard.

trials.name: mRNA-4157 + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-942)
trials.takeaway: Proof of concept for individualised cancer vaccines.

appraisal.critique: Personalised neoantigen vaccine with pembrolizumab improves RFS in resected melanoma. It is phase 2; phase 3 (INTerpath-001) has since reported.

trials.name: Cemiplimab cSCC / Avelumab Merkel
trials.population: Advanced cutaneous SCC / Merkel cell carcinoma
trials.result: cSCC ORR ~47%; Merkel ORR ~33% (2L), higher first line
trials.takeaway: Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 is standard for advanced cSCC and Merkel cell carcinoma.

inclusion: Advanced cutaneous SCC / Merkel cell carcinoma
appraisal.critique: Immunotherapy gives high, durable response rates in advanced cSCC and Merkel cell carcinoma. Data are single-arm, and transplant recipients are at risk of rejection.

trials.name: ACOSOG Z9001 / SSG XVIII
trials.takeaway: Three years of adjuvant imatinib for high-risk GIST (KIT exon 11 most benefit; not PDGFRA D842V).

appraisal.critique: Three years of adjuvant imatinib improves OS over one year in high-risk GIST. Optimal duration beyond three years is under study.

trials.name: B2222 / EORTC 62005
trials.takeaway: Imatinib 400 mg first line; 800 mg for KIT exon 9.

appraisal.critique: Imatinib 400 mg is standard for advanced GIST, with 800 mg for KIT exon 9 mutations. Resistance develops over time.

trials.name: INVICTUS / VOYAGER
trials.population: Advanced GIST after ≥3 TKIs (INVICTUS); PDGFRA D842V (NAVIGATOR)
trials.takeaway: Ripretinib fourth line; avapritinib for PDGFRA D842V.

inclusion: Advanced GIST after ≥3 TKIs (INVICTUS); PDGFRA D842V (NAVIGATOR)
appraisal.critique: Ripretinib improves OS as fourth-line therapy in GIST. Avapritinib is effective for PDGFRA D842V.

trials.name: O'Sullivan NCIC SR2
trials.result: Wound complications 35% vs 17%; less fibrosis/oedema with preop; similar local control
trials.takeaway: Preoperative RT is preferred (lower dose, less late toxicity).

appraisal.critique: Preoperative RT causes less fibrosis and oedema than postoperative RT but more wound complications. Preoperative RT is preferred for extremity sarcoma.

trials.name: STRASS
trials.result: No overall benefit; possible benefit in liposarcoma
trials.takeaway: Preoperative RT is not routine for retroperitoneal sarcoma.

appraisal.critique: Preoperative RT did not improve abdominal recurrence-free survival in retroperitoneal sarcoma overall. Liposarcoma may benefit.

trials.name: EORTC 62012
trials.result: OS not significantly improved (14.3 vs 12.8 mo); higher ORR and PFS
trials.takeaway: Single-agent doxorubicin is first line; combination when response needed.

appraisal.critique: Doxorubicin + ifosfamide improves response but not OS over doxorubicin alone. The combination is used when response is needed for symptom control or surgery.

trials.name: EURAMOS-1
trials.result: No benefit from intensifying for poor responders
trials.takeaway: MAP remains standard for osteosarcoma.

appraisal.critique: Intensifying chemotherapy for poor responders did not improve outcomes in osteosarcoma. MAP remains standard.

trials.name: EURO EWING 2012 / rEECur
trials.takeaway: VDC/IE is the preferred regimen.

appraisal.critique: VDC/IE improves OS over VIDE in Ewing sarcoma. Interval compression requires G-CSF.

trials.name: Hartsell RTOG 97-14
trials.takeaway: 8 Gy single fraction is standard for uncomplicated bone pain.

appraisal.critique: A single 8 Gy fraction gives equal pain relief to 30 Gy/10 for bone metastases. Higher retreatment rates are acceptable for convenience.

trials.name: SC.24 (spine SBRT)
trials.takeaway: Spine SBRT gives more complete pain response in selected patients.

appraisal.critique: SBRT improves complete pain response for spinal metastases. Fracture risk and technology requirements limit use.

trials.name: Patchell MSCC
trials.result: Ambulatory 84% vs 57%; retained ambulation 122 vs 13 days
trials.takeaway: Surgery + RT for suitable patients with MSCC.

appraisal.critique: Surgery plus RT improves ambulation over RT alone for MSCC. Patient selection is key.

trials.name: SCORAD III
trials.result: Ambulatory status ~70% in both arms; non-inferiority margin narrowly not met
trials.takeaway: Single 8 Gy is reasonable for patients with short expected survival.

appraisal.critique: A single 8 Gy fraction is non-inferior to 20 Gy/5 for ambulation in MSCC. It is appropriate for patients with short life expectancy.

trials.name: ORIOLE / STOMP
trials.takeaway: Metastasis-directed therapy can delay ADT in oligorecurrent prostate cancer.

appraisal.critique: Metastasis-directed therapy delays ADT in oligometastatic prostate cancer. Larger trials are needed.

trials.name: Navari olanzapine CINV
trials.takeaway: Four-drug antiemetic prophylaxis (olanzapine 5–10 mg) for HEC.

appraisal.critique: Olanzapine 10 mg improves nausea control with HEC. Sedation is common; 5 mg may suffice.

trials.name: Hokusai VTE Cancer / SELECT-D / Caravaggio
trials.result: DOACs non-inferior to LMWH; more GI/GU bleeding with edoxaban/rivaroxaban
trials.takeaway: DOACs are standard for cancer-associated VTE except high GI/GU bleeding risk.

limitations: Higher GI bleeding with some DOACs
appraisal.critique: DOACs are non-inferior to LMWH for cancer-associated VTE. Higher GI bleeding with edoxaban and rivaroxaban in GI cancers requires caution.

trials.name: Denosumab vs zoledronic acid (Stopeck / Fizazi)
trials.result: Delayed first SRE (prostate HR 0.82); similar OS; ONJ ~2%
trials.takeaway: Bone-modifying agents reduce SREs; check dental health and calcium.

appraisal.critique: Denosumab reduces skeletal events more than zoledronic acid. It does not improve OS, and hypocalcaemia and cost are concerns.

trials.name: ABCSG-18 / Early Breast EBCTCG bisphosphonates
trials.result: Bisphosphonates reduce bone recurrence and BC death in postmenopausal women
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant zoledronic acid for postmenopausal higher-risk early BC.

appraisal.critique: Adjuvant bisphosphonates reduce fractures and recurrence in postmenopausal early breast cancer. Osteonecrosis of the jaw is rare but serious.
